sentences.text: Plesiolophus is known from a partial skull that defines the single species P. warnerensis.
These remains constitute the first diagnostic adult lambeosaurine material recovered from the Oldman Formation.
The fossils were uncovered by Wendy Sloboda near Warner, Alberta, Canada.
The holotype—the specimen on which the species is based—is curated at the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology under accession TMP 2016.023.0039.
Plesiolophus belongs to the family Hadrosauridae, the duck-billed herbivores.
Within Hadrosauridae it is placed in the tribe Parasaurolophini, a group of lambeosaurine hadrosaurs.
Phylogenetic analysis indicates it is the basalmost member of an exclusively North American clade of Parasaurolophini.
Higher-level classification places Plesiolophus in the ornithischian class, the bird-hipped dinosaurs.
Plesiolophus lived during the Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
Its fossils come from the Oldman Formation, a sedimentary unit that underlies the Dinosaur Park Formation.
